reply: A shallow copy copies only the top level of a structure. Any nested objects are references, so two copies share them. A deep copy makes new objects at every level, so they diverge completely.

It pairs two sequences element-by-element.

```python
list(zip([1, 2, 3], ['a', 'b', 'c']))
# [(1, 'a'), (2, 'b'), (3, 'c')]
```

It stops at the shortest one.

`arr.length` is the property.

```js
const arr = [1, 2, 3];
arr.length; // 3
```

It works for arrays and for strings (`"abc".length` is 3). For objects, `Object.keys(obj).length` is the number of properties.

Reliability and resale are the two numbers that drive the used-car purchase, so start there. For a compact, a Honda Civic and Toyota Corolla are the consistent choice: they hold value and when they're not being repaired, they're not being repaired. For a midsize, a Camry or Accord — both are workhorses with parts everywhere. For SUVs, a RAV4 or CR-V are the safe bets; if budget is tight, a Hyundai Elantra or Kona will often be cheaper than the Honda/Toyota equivalent and have similar durability.

A Ford F-150 will still be supported for years of parts, but it's more expensive to own than the Japanese pickups. If you like trucks, an older Tacoma or Tundra is far better long-term than current-year Fords.

Condition matters more than brand for used cars. A 10-year-old Japanese compact in good history is better than a 3-year-old American luxury car with no history. Get a third-party inspection before buying anything above $5,000 — $200 is cheap insurance against a $2,000 repair. A quick history check at CARFAX or your county's motor vehicle office will show whether it was in an accident or had major repairs.

Budget builds split cleanly into two: integrated graphics and entry discrete cards. Integrated is only worth it if you have enough CPU cores and don't need above 1080p. Intel Core Ultra 200-series APU is the current best of that group, and AMD's Ryzen 7000/8000 APU is the older but still good option. If you do want a card, the cheapest reasonable option is RX 6400. It handles 1440p light titles well and scales to 4K with DLSS/FSR, but its single-big-card footprint means it competes best against itself. An RX 6550 or a GTX 1650 would be better than a 6400, both for performance and power draw.
